messages:
morgan: Taking prim for the next hour — heads up we're seeing p95/p99 spikes for hosted text-gen in us-west-2. Alerts are noisy but customer-facing 5xx rate is still low. paging might start if p99 stays > 1.2s :eyes:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED: model-serving-high-p99 in channel eng-oncall — Priority P2 — Pager: oncall-primary — Trigger: p99 > 1.2s sustained 3m — Incident ID INC-2143
ravi: on it. can you dump recent tail of the serving logs for the affected shards? curious if it's latency or queueing/backpressure
morgan: pasted a quick grep below for last 2min (shard-id masked). spikes correspond to a handful of model-worker GC pauses + queue length bump:
```
2026-03-15T18:07:12Z worker-43 INFO queue_len=12 req_latency=0.55s
2026-03-15T18:07:18Z worker-43 WARN gc_pause=1.1s
2026-03-15T18:07:20Z worker-12 INFO queue_len=17 req_latency=0.9s
2026-03-15T18:07:25Z worker-43 INFO req_latency=1.45s p99
```
jamal: ok GC on some workers — likely noisy co-tenancy on that node pool. Are we still routing traffic to the canary variant?
sophie: quick checklist from runbook: 1) confirm model fallback is enabled, 2) check autoscaler add capacity, 3) if customer impact > threshold do regional route shift. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-latency-throttle
ravi: can you run the autoscaler probe and check nodepool utilization? `rboxctl nodepool describe us-west-2-gen` and `rboxctl asg metrics --pool gen-usw2`
morgan: running probes now. nodepool at 78% CPU, burst headroom limited. autoscaler shows 0 pending scale-ups (failed to trigger last 10m). I'm going to force a scale-up per runbook step 4 to buy time: `rboxctl autoscale force-up --pool gen-usw2 --nodes 3`
incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: user morgan invoked autoscale force-up for gen-usw2 +3 nodes — INC-2143
jamal: while that lands, I'd prefer to reduce tail risk by enabling the less-accurate but faster quantized variant (fallback). How to flip safely?
sophie: variant switch is a per-route config. quick command (non-prod tested):
```bash
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --model redwood-lg-quant-v2 --region us-west-2 --weight 0.2
```
this keeps 80% on prod model. runbook recommends 10-30% weight for progressive fallback. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/variant-fallback
ravi: notifying support to watch for customer complaints. @oncall-bridge can you patch the customer-impact doc w/ current status?
oncall-bridge: noted, updating impact doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2143/status — current CI: degraded latency for hosted text-gen in us-west-2, error rate normal. adding runbook links and mitigation steps.
morgan: forced autoscale succeeded — +3 nodes in 90s, worker GC settled on new nodes. p99 dropped to 0.6s after scale. keeping fallback at 10% for 5m to observe.
incident-bot: UPDATE: p99 back to 0.62s avg over 60s window — closing immediate alert condition. ACTION: monitor 15m.
jamal: nice. quick post-handoff notes for whoever takes next: - check nodepool autoscale logs for the 10m before the incident (failed scale attempts); - look at GC alloc patterns on worker-43; - consider pinning high-traffic customers to dedicated capacity if repeat.
sophie: adding exact runbook pointers to the incident card: model-latency-throttle, variant-fallback, autoscale-troubleshoot. Also: snippet to restart a single worker if it misbehaves: `kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/model-worker-43` (use with caution).
morgan: handing to ravi for the next 30m observation window — I'll stay reachable for 10. ravi, you're primary now.
ravi: taking primary. I'll keep an eye on INC-2143 and triage the autoscaler logs. thanks for the handoff. emoji :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: Primary changed to ravi — On-call handoff logged. NOTE: watch window until 1768301310
morgan: thanks team — closing my handoff. if anything flares ping me or escalate to SRE lead. :lock:
internal_note: handoff thread with runbook links, autoscale action, variant fallback, and quick remediation snippets
